Biigtigong Nishnaabeg

Biigtigong Nishnaabeg is an Ojibway community at the mouth of the Pic River on Lake Superior. Its own public accounts connect waterways, fishing, community education and responsibilities to future generations. These sources provide a starting point without settling territorial or legal claims.

These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

Fishing and community education

Biigtigong’s2016 Fisheries Act submission describes fishing as a source of food, knowledge and connection. In its selected education discussion, the Nation says it began changing school curriculum in2014 to include land-based activities and held a community fish camp in2016 at the mouth of the Pic River. The account explains why learning across generations matters to the community. It is a dated primary submission, not evidence that every later education goal was completed.

Read the sources [1] Biigtigong Nishnaabeg; hosted by the House of Commons

02

Waterways and stewardship

The2026 ICCA Registry case study presents the custodians’ account of relationships with six waterways, including the Pic River. It describes efforts to involve the community in stewardship, reconnect younger generations with waterways and develop locally directed monitoring. The registry explicitly calls the initiative self-declared and not yet peer-reviewed. Readers should distinguish those community goals and interpretations from independently established legal recognition, surveyed boundaries or verified environmental outcomes.

Read the sources [2] Biigtigong Nishnaabeg custodians / UNEP-WCMC ICCA Registry
